title: How Handy met Johnny Richards over 'Bahia'; the Neophonics
summary: Handy phoned Richards after hearing 'Bahia'; Schremp explains Joel Kaye's Neophonics.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: I recall things that he wrote, oh Lord, before I joined the Raeburn band. I think I met John a little before that. He had his own band in those days in New York and boy, I went up to a publisher's office one day, the guy said, have you heard the Johnny Richards' band lately? I said no. He said, I have a copy here of one of his new charts on a tune called 'Bahia'; do you remember that tune?
I think I have that chart.
Really?
Not the original, but a printed copy of it.
Some of that stuff was later issued by Berkeley School. I think I have "Bahia".

I just love that chart, and I said to this publisher, how can I get in touch with him, and he said he's staying at Hotel so and so. Do you have his number? Yeah. I called him from the office right there, you don't know me, my name is George Handy, I just heard your chart of "Bahia" and I think it's one of the most marvelous--that's how we met, on the phone.
I had to tell him how much I thought of that tune. It was really great. We became friends after that.
Do you know Joel Kaye? I'm sure you know Joel Kaye.
The drummer?
No, he's a saxophone player. He played bass with Kenton for a while. Joel is Johnny Richards' sort of
godson and--what the hell is it called--a great pompous name for a jazz group in New York--
Neophonics?
The Neophonics.
Joel gave Neophonic. That's the continuation of the Johnny Richards' band.
Oh, terrific. He has those charts?

He has the charts and I don't think he plays them anymore, but he has them and he was literally adopted by, I think, Richards. He's the godson or whatever. Not godson--what am I trying to say--foster son, perhaps informally.
That's where that road ran to.
Right.
That's the band that Jack McKenney said you should look up, because they wanted you to write for them. That was about a year or two ago.
